qs.q: A patient with mucormycosis presents with a black eschar. The organism is identified by which morphological feature?
o: Narrow, septate hyphae branching at acute angles
Broad, aseptate hyphae branching at right angles
Yeast cells with thick, double‑contoured walls
Mold producing conidiophores that bear phialides
qs.e: Mucorales appear as broad, non-septate hyphae with right-angle branching.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with mucormycosis presents with rhinocerebral disease. The organism is identified by which morphological feature?
o: Narrow, septate hyphae with acute-angle branching
Yeast cells possessing thick, double-contoured walls
Broad, non-septate hyphae with right-angle branching
qs.e: Mucorales appear as broad, non-septate hyphae with right-angle branching.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A clinical sample reveals broad, non-septate hyphae branching at wide angles in a patient with rhino-orbital mucormycosis. Which drug class is clinically indicated as first-line empirical therapy?
o: Polyenes binding to cell membrane ergosterol
qs.e: Zygomycetes causing mucormycosis are uniquely susceptible to polyenes like amphotericin B among systemic agents.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which factor is most directly associated with the re-emergence of mucormycosis during the COVID-19 pandemic?
o: Universal adoption of immunosuppressive biologic therapies
Widespread use of corticosteroids in diabetic patients
Massive administration of broad-spectrum antibacterial drugs
Global travel spreading endemic spores from the desert
qs.e: Mucormycosis re-emerged significantly during the COVID-19 pandemic particularly in diabetic patients on corticosteroids. These risk factors create a favorable environment for opportunistic fungal invasion.
